texts.preamble: Birendra Prasad Singh And Anr vs The State Of Jharkhand on 5 May, 2016 Author: Rongon Mukhopadhyay Bench: Rongon Mukhopadhyay In The High Court Of Jharkhand At Ranchi Cr.M.P. No. 1249 of 2014 ---- 1. Birendra Prasad Singh, Son of late K.P. Singh, Resident of 6, Old T.C. Colony, I.C. Road, P.O. & P.S. Kadma, Town-Jamshedpur, District-East Singhbhum. 2. Man Singh, Son of Sri Ram Singh, Resident of 39, Nanak Nagar, Namda Basti, P.O. & P.S. Golmuri, Town-Jamshedpur, District- East Singhbhum. ........Petitioners Versus The State of Jharkhand. ....Opposite Party -------- Coram: The Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Rongon Mukhopadhyay -------- For the Petitioners : Mr. Amit Kumar Das, Advocate For the State : Mr. Azeemuddin, App --------
texts.facts: The petitioners in this application have prayed for quashing the entire criminal proceeding in connection with C-2 Case No.512 of 2013 including the order dated 12.02.2013 (12.02.2014), passed by the learned Judicial Magistrate, 1st class, Jamshedpur, whereby and whereunder cognizance has been taken for the offence punishable under section 59 of the Food Safety & Standard Act, 2006 ( hereinafter referred to as the Act) The allegation made in the prosecution report is to the effect that the Investigating Officer, designated under the Act, had collected sample of "Catch" Haldi (Turmeric) Powder from the store of M/s Steel Workers' Welfare Society as the same did not conform to the Food Safety & Standards Rules, 2011. On making an analysis, the same was found to be adulterated and unsafe due to presence of 'lead chromate', which is a harmful toxic substance and accordingly prosecution was sought for against the petitioners as well as suppliers and manufacturers.
texts.arguments: It has been submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioners that petitioner no. 1 is the Secretary of M/s Steel Workers' Welfare Society and petitioner no. 2 is the Store In-charge. Learned counsel submits that admittedly the petitioners can be termed to be sellers and in view of section 27 of the Act since none of the conditions are fulfilled so as to prosecute the petitioners, the entire Birendra Prasad Singh And Anr vs The State Of Jharkhand on 5 May, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75353048/ 1 proceedings deserves to be [LEAKAGE_MASK] and [LEAKAGE_MASK]. Learned counsel has referred to Section 67 of the Act and has submitted that the society of the petitioners also comes within the definition of a Company as per explanation to Section 67 and the society having not been made an accused, the petitioners cannot be made vicariously liable. Learned A.P.P. has submitted that "Catch" Haldi (Turmeric) Powder was seized from the store of the petitioners and from the report of Food Analyst, it appears that the same does not conform to the prescribed standard of quality specified under the FS&S Regulation-2011 due to presence of lead chromate. It has been submitted that sanction for launching prosecution had also been given by the Commissioner of Food Safety cum Principal Secretary, Department of Health, Family Welfare and Medical Education, Government of Jharkhand. Learned APP thus submits that the petitioners can be directly responsible for keeping food products, which does not conform to the prescribed standard and procedure as laid down under the Acts, Rules & Regulations framed thereunder. In order to appreciate the rival contention, it would be necessary to consider Section 27 of the Act, which reads as follows:- 27. Liability of Manufacturers, packers, wholesalers, distributors and sellers.- "(1) The manufacturer or packer of an article of food shall be liable for such article of food if it does not meet the requirements of this Act and the rules and regulations made thereunder. (2) The wholesaler or distributor shall be liable under this Act for any article of food which is- (a) supplied after the date of its expiry; or (b) stored or supplied in violation of the safety instructions of the manufacturer; or (c) unsafe or misbranded, or (d) unidentifiable of manufacturer from whom the article of food have been received; or (e) stored or handled or kept in violation of the provisions of this Act, the rules and regulations made thereunder; or (f) received by him with knowledge of being unsafe. (3) The seller shall be liable under this Act, for any article of food which is- (a) sold after the date of its expiry; or (b) handled or kept in unhygienic conditions; or (c) misbranded; or Birendra Prasad Singh And Anr vs The State Of Jharkhand on 5 May, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75353048/ 2 (d) unidentifiable of the manufacturer or the distributors from whom such articles of food were received; or (e) received by him with knowledge of being unsafe". Section 27 in different parts fixes liability upon manufacturers, packers, wholesalers, distributors and the sellers in facts situation which does not meet the requirement under the Act.
